About Smartfire

Smartfire is self-hosted, open-source team chat. Each workspace runs on its own server, operated by the organization that set it up, and that organization controls its workspace's data.

What you can do here

  • Talk in rooms organized by topic or team, with threads for side conversations.
  • Share files, both uploads stored on the workspace server and Google Drive links.
  • Plan with room events, and optionally publish your Going and Maybe RSVPs to your own Google Calendar.
  • Meet over voice and video huddles without leaving the room.
  • Connect optional integrations your workspace enables, such as GitHub pull-request cards, bots, and agents.

Signing in with Google

Where the workspace enables it, members can sign in with their Google Workspace account. Google sign-in only verifies your identity: it does not connect your calendar or your Drive files. Connecting Google Calendar or Drive previews is a separate, optional choice you make later from your profile.

Your data stays with this workspace

Messages you post, including direct messages, and files you upload are stored on this workspace's server and may remain in its backups. People who operate that server can access that data. Room membership still controls what ordinary members can see. The privacy policy explains this in detail; the terms of service covers the rules for using the workspace.

Privacy Policy

Last updated: September 18, 2026

Smartfire is self-hosted software. This policy describes how the workspace you use handles your data. The organization hosting your workspace controls that data; the people who build Smartfire do not receive your workspace's content simply because you use the software.

Contractors and guests, please note: everything you post in this workspace, including direct messages, is stored on the workspace's server, may remain in its backups, and can be accessible to the people who operate that server. It does not disappear automatically when you leave. Room permissions limit what ordinary members can see, but they are not end-to-end encryption and are not a privacy guarantee against the hosting organization.

Data this workspace stores

  • Account and profile: your name, email address, avatar, role, and room memberships. Password sign-in stores a password verifier, never your plain password.
  • Workspace content: messages in rooms, threads, and direct messages, reactions, and files you upload, which are stored on the workspace's server. Content you post in a room is visible to that room's members; direct messages are visible to their participants.
  • Sign-in and device data: a session cookie that keeps you signed in, interface preferences kept in your browser, and, where you enable them, installed-app (PWA) data and push-notification subscriptions.
  • Connection and security records: IP addresses, browser and device information, and operational logs used to run the service, investigate abuse, and keep accounts secure.

Who can see workspace content

  • Room members can see content posted in rooms they belong to.
  • Workspace administrators manage accounts and workspace settings. That role alone does not let them open private rooms or direct messages they do not belong to through Smartfire's interface.
  • People with access to the server, database, or backups can access stored workspace data, including direct messages and uploaded files. This infrastructure access is separate from room membership and the application's administrator role.
  • Configured bots, agents, and webhooks can receive messages and attachment links in rooms they belong to, limited by their capability grants.

The public pages describing Smartfire (About, Privacy, Terms) set no tracking cookies and load no analytics.

Optional integrations

  • GitHub: where enabled, pasting a pull-request link shows a live card fetched from GitHub; members who link their own GitHub account can act on pull requests as themselves. Room subscriptions can post repository events into rooms.
  • Huddles: voice and video calls connect through the real-time media server configured for the workspace. Call preferences, such as device choices, are kept in your browser.
  • Error diagnostics: the workspace operator may configure error reporting (Sentry) for its own deployment. When configured, crash reports go to the operator's error-reporting account. Reports can include selected record fields, including message text when a message cannot be displayed, as well as error and request details. Default personal data collection is left off, but that does not exclude these diagnostic fields.

Hosting, backup, and media providers depend on the organization running your workspace; this policy makes no promise about specific vendors or regions.

Signing in with Google

Where the workspace enables Google sign-in, Google verifies your identity and Smartfire receives your stable Google account identifier, your verified email address and Workspace domain, and your name for setting up your profile. The request uses only the openid email profile scopes. No Google access tokens or refresh tokens from sign-in are kept. Google sign-in never connects your calendar or your Drive files.

Google Calendar (optional)

Connecting Google Calendar from your profile is opt-in. Smartfire keeps your encrypted access and refresh tokens, your connection email address, and the granted scopes on the workspace server, and writes private copies of Smartfire events you are Going to or Maybe attending onto your primary Google Calendar, including the title, description, time, and meeting links. Publishing is one way: Smartfire never reads your event titles, descriptions, locations, or attendee lists, and changes you make in Google do not sync back. If you separately opt into "Show when I'm in a meeting", Smartfire also reads the start and end times of events on your primary calendar (declined, all-day, out-of-office, and "free" events excluded) to derive your on/off meeting state; only that state is ever shown to other members, and opting out or disconnecting deletes the stored times. If you opt into "Use my Google Calendar out-of-office", Smartfire reads the type, start, and end of your out-of-office events to derive your out-of-office state and return date; only that state, the date, and a note you write yourself are ever shown to other members.

Disconnecting removes the connection and its local entries from the workspace server and attempts to remove the calendar copies it created, though some remote copies may remain for you to delete. Your Google sign-in link is separate and stays in place. You can also revoke access any time from your Google Account connections page; revoking stops future access but does not delete events already created, file grants already made, messages already posted, or your sign-in identity.

Google Drive (optional)

Where enabled, Drive links render as chips. Files you picked through Smartfire's file picker can show a preview chip (file name, type, owner display name, modified time, and link) resolved at view time with the viewer's own Google credentials under per-file consent: Smartfire can only see files you opened with it, never your whole Drive. Pasted links to anything else show a plain chip naming only the file kind (such as "Google Doc"), with no metadata lookup. Preview metadata is cached briefly (about five minutes) per viewer and never shared across members. Attaching a Drive file to a message stores only the file's ID on the workspace server, never its name or contents.

The file-sharing picker works entirely in your browser with per-file consent: it uses a short-lived token kept only in browser memory, never the tokens stored on the server for Calendar. It reads the selected file's details, whether you may share it, and the existing permission list, then grants reader access only to the current room members you explicitly choose, keeps any stronger access they already have, and sends no Google sharing notification emails. Grants apply immediately and stay in place even if you never send the message or a recipient later leaves; later members are not added automatically.

These Drive features never download or store your file contents; files you upload directly to Smartfire are a separate feature stored on the workspace server. Google's own policies apply to Google's services.

How Google user data is protected

Data obtained through Google's sign-in, Calendar, and Drive scopes is used only to provide the visible features described above, to keep the service secure, and as the law requires. It is not sold, not used for advertising, not used to judge credit or lending applications, and not used to train general-purpose AI models. People may read Google user data only with your affirmative agreement to view specific data, when necessary for security or legal compliance, or for internal operations using aggregated, anonymized data as Google's Limited Use requirements permit. Infrastructure access does not authorize additional uses of Google user data. Drive attachments are shared with configured room bots and agents only as file IDs and links under their existing room access, never as Google credentials or file contents. Smartfire follows Google's API Services User Data Policy, including its Limited Use requirements.

Retention and deletion

The workspace keeps messages, uploads, and account data until they are removed. The hosting organization decides retention and backup practices for its workspace, so copies may persist in backups after visible content is deleted, and there is no promise of instant or complete deletion everywhere. Leaving the workspace or having your account deactivated does not automatically delete your messages, uploads, or backup copies. To ask about access, correction, or deletion of your data, contact the organization hosting your workspace, which handles such requests subject to its legal and business obligations.

Contact

This workspace is operated by the organization hosting it. Your workspace administrator can tell you who that is.

Direct privacy questions to your workspace administrator.
